title.value: Predicting histopathology markers of endometrial carcinoma with a quantitative image analysis approach based on spherical harmonics in multiparametric MRI
title.justification: The title accurately describes the focus of the paper on using spherical harmonics in MRI to predict histopathology markers of endometrial carcinoma.
title.quote: Predicting histopathology markers of endometrial carcinoma with a quantitative image analysis approach based on spherical harmonics in multiparametric MRI

extractions.description: The paper introduces a machine learning framework using spherical harmonics (SPHARM) for predicting histopathology markers of endometrial carcinoma through multiparametric MRI. It compares the diagnostic performance of SPHARM analysis with traditional radiomics in predicting deep myometrial invasion and tumor high-grade status. The study involves a retrospective analysis of MRI data from different institutions, emphasizing the accuracy and robustness of the SPHARM method over conventional techniques.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper primarily focuses on medical imaging and machine learning techniques for cancer diagnosis rather than addressing climate or ecological sustainable development.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Purpose: Identifying optimal machine learning pipelines for computer-aided diagnosis is key for the development of robust, reproducible, and clinically relevant imaging biomarkers for endometrial carcinoma.

applications.justification: The specific application of the paper is in the field of medical imaging for diagnosing endometrial carcinoma using advanced imaging analysis techniques.
applications.quote: The purpose of this study was to introduce the mathematical development of image descriptors computed from spherical harmonics (SPHARM) decompositions as well as the associated machine learning pipeline, and to evaluate their performance in predicting deep myometrial invasion (MI) and histopathological high-grade in preoperative multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).
